questions.q: In the lifecycle run, the candidate retrained on weeks 5 and 6 beat the champion on weeks 7 and 8 (AUC 0.593 vs 0.529) but was still blocked. Why?
options: The gate only accepts models trained on the original data
The contract test failed
MLflow refused to register it
It was still below the absolute floors (AUC 0.70, average precision 0.25), so it is not good enough to ship even though it is better
questions.explain: A gate combines rules. Beating a decayed champion is not enough when the candidate is far below the floors, and the blocked cycle tells a person that retraining alone did not repair the model.

questions.q: Why did the capstone run drills that injected shuffled labels and a percentage-returning model?
options: To improve the model's accuracy
To reduce the training time
To see the safety checks actually fail, because a check you have never seen fail is only a guess
To fill the MLflow registry with versions
questions.explain: Injecting known faults proves the gate and contract test catch real problems, and that the champion alias does not move when they fire.

questions.q: What is the honest status of the GitHub Actions workflow in this capstone?
options: It was run on GitHub and passed
It was checked to parse as valid YAML but was not run on GitHub, so action versions and runner details need checking
It was run locally with Docker
It is not relevant to the project
questions.explain: Everything in the pipeline ran locally. The workflow is illustrative: it parses, but it was never executed on GitHub.

questions.q: The scheduled refresh candidate scored AUC 0.780 against the champion's 0.789 and was promoted. Why?
options: The difference of 0.009 is within the 0.01 max_drop tolerance, which is a policy choice a team can tighten
The gate does not compare with the champion
Lower AUC is always better
The contract test overrides the gate
questions.explain: The gate blocks candidates worse than the champion by more than 0.01 AUC. Setting max_drop to 0 would require the candidate to be at least as good.

questions.q: Which is the best way to present this project in a portfolio?
options: Show only the successful runs and hide the limitations
Present it as a production system serving real customers
Lead with a README, show the failures the gates caught, attach the model card, and mark what is simulated or unrun
Submit only the trained model file
questions.explain: Reviewers trust work that states its limits. Blocked candidates and drills demonstrate the safety checks, and labelling simulated data and unrun CI keeps claims honest.
